classification.classification_note: ARVO metadata marks this sample unclassified; the staged vulnerable source and AddressSanitizer trace ground a stale default-listener pointer dereference after listener-array reallocation.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists where a mixed default/non-default listener configuration in the listener config could cause a crash on startup. This affects only very unusual configurations.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 191-byte config witness with SHA-256 `b27a4c116ea3223c5afab4eca398e5175b6f9c2f5529b58dbf89f8f464c610f6` begins with the nonblank line `crlfile listene1r 892`, later contains `listener tene1r 892`, and later a bare `port` line. When `config__read_file_core()` tokenizes the first `crlfile` option with no current listener, `REQUIRE_LISTENER_OR_DEFAULT_LISTENER` calls `config__create_default_listener()`, which allocates the first `config->listeners` array element and stores `config->default_listener = &config->listeners[0]`. The later `listener tene1r 892` line is not rejected: `conf__parse_int()` consumes `tene1r`, `atoi()` converts it to `tmp_int = 0`, and the saved vulnerable build enables `WITH_UNIX_SOCKETS`, so the `listener` validation path accepts port 0 when the following token `892` is present as a Unix-socket path. That accepted explicit-listener path reaches `config__add_listener()` again; AddressSanitizer shows the second `mosquitto__realloc()` at `src/conf.c:149` frees the old 224-byte one-listener array while growing it. Because the vulnerable code does not remap `config->default_listener` after that realloc, a later `port` option reuses the stale non-null pointer; `config__create_default_listener()` returns immediately and `if(config->default_listener->port)` reads freed memory at `src/conf.c:2098`. The fix records the default-listener index before realloc and restores `config->default_listener` afterward.

source.description: First project statement that materializes vulnerability-relevant parser state from the attacker-controlled config text. On the crashing path it turns the first nonblank line into option token `crlfile`, which is the key that can create a default listener before any explicit listener exists.
source.value_from: The staged 191-byte config witness in `gt_results/arvo_55886/poc` has SHA-256 `b27a4c116ea3223c5afab4eca398e5175b6f9c2f5529b58dbf89f8f464c610f6`. Its first nonblank line is `crlfile listene1r 892`; later nonblank lines include `listener tene1r 892` and bare `port`.
source.note: The libFuzzer entry only writes bytes to a temporary `.conf` file. This option-tokenization statement is the scored project parser boundary.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `port` handling reuses the stale `config->default_listener` alias and reads its `port` field after the old listener array has already been freed by `config__add_listener()`.
sink.note: The saved run reports `READ of size 2` and `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free /src/mosquitto/src/conf.c:2098:35 in config__read_file_core`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The second listener addition grows `config->listeners` with `realloc()`, which may free and move the old array, but the vulnerable code does not repair `config->default_listener`, a raw pointer that still aliases the first array element.
root_cause.note: The fixing patch wraps this realloc with default-listener index bookkeeping and rebinds `config->default_listener` after growth; the ASan free stack also points to this exact line on the second `config__add_listener()` call.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment creates the long-lived alias later used by the `port` option. It stores a raw pointer into the listener array rather than a stable index or handle, so later array growth can invalidate it.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: This alias is created immediately after the first `crlfile`-driven call to `config__add_listener()` allocates the one-listener array.
tainted_value_origin.note: After the first default-listener creation, this pointer names `config->listeners[0]`; step 8 leaves that same alias dangling.

parser_admitted.description: After newline stripping and blank/comment skipping, the config reader tokenizes each nonblank line into an option name and enters the option-dispatch chain. The witness reaches this parser and yields `crlfile` as its first relevant token.

coarse_trace.summary: The first nonblank `crlfile` option is parsed with no active listener, so Mosquitto allocates the initial one-element `config->listeners` array and stores `config->default_listener` as a pointer to that first element.

A later `listener tene1r 892` line is parsed into `tmp_int = 0` because `conf__parse_int()` uses `atoi()` on `tene1r`; with `-DWITH_UNIX_SOCKETS`, port 0 plus following token `892` is accepted as a Unix-socket listener, so `config__add_listener()` reallocates the listener array and frees the old one-element storage without repairing `config->default_listener`.

A later bare `port` option enters the default-listener path, keeps the stale non-null alias, and dereferences `config->default_listener->port`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free at line 2098.

fine_trace.note: The vulnerable parser reads attacker-controlled configuration lines into `*buf`. On the witnessed path, the relevant nonblank lines later tokenized at steps 1, 4, and 9 are `crlfile listene1r 892`, `listener tene1r 892`, and bare `port`.
Source step. After blank-line stripping, the first relevant line is tokenized and `token` becomes `crlfile`, the option name that can create a default listener when no listener has been selected yet.

Handling that first `crlfile` token reaches `config__create_default_listener()`, which calls `config__add_listener()`. On this first call, `mosquitto__realloc()` grows `NULL` to a one-element listener array, the same 224-byte region that ASan later reports as the original allocation.
The newly created default listener is stored as a raw alias to the first array element. Later `port` handling will reuse this pointer instead of re-deriving the listener after array growth.
A later nonblank witness line is tokenized as option name `listener` from `listener tene1r 892`, which selects the explicit-listener parsing branch.

`conf__parse_int()` consumes the next token from `listener tene1r 892`. It reads `tene1r`, and `atoi()` converts that malformed token to `tmp_int = 0`, which becomes the listener port value seen by the caller.

The saved vulnerable build compiles with `-DWITH_UNIX_SOCKETS`, so this branch uses the lower bound `tmp_int < 0` instead of `tmp_int < 1`. The converted value `tmp_int = 0` therefore survives the port-range check here.

The same listener line yields a third token `892`. Because `tmp_int == 0` and this token is non-NULL, the `if(tmp_int == 0 && token == NULL)` guard at lines 1716-1718 does not reject the line, so the parser accepts it as a Unix-socket listener definition.

Root-cause step. On this startup parse (`reload == false`), the accepted explicit-listener branch reaches `config__read_file_core():1763` and calls `config__add_listener()` a second time. `mosquitto__realloc()` grows the array to two listeners and frees the old one-element region; AddressSanitizer records this exact free stack. `config->default_listener` is not updated, so it now dangles on the freed first element.

A later nonblank witness line is tokenized as option name `port` from the bare line `port`. No numeric argument has been parsed yet; the deprecated default-listener branch will first consult `config->default_listener`.

Sink step. In the `port` branch, `config__create_default_listener(config, token)` at line 2095 returns immediately because `config->default_listener` is non-null, even though step 8 left it stale. This `if(config->default_listener->port)` test therefore reads the freed first listener's `port` field, matching AddressSanitizer's heap-use-after-free `READ of size 2` at this line.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` reproduces the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free when `broker_fuzz_test_config` writes the bytes to a temporary config file and runs Mosquitto with `--test-config -c <file>`; the crash occurs during `config__read_file_core()` after the leading `crlfile` creates a default listener, `listener tene1r 892` is accepted as a Unix-socket listener in the staged `-DWITH_UNIX_SOCKETS` build, and a later bare `port` reuses the stale default-listener pointer.

format.contract: The exact staged 191-byte text witness with SHA-256 `b27a4c116ea3223c5afab4eca398e5175b6f9c2f5529b58dbf89f8f464c610f6`. Its vulnerability-relevant nonblank option sequence is `crlfile listene1r 892`, later `listener tene1r 892`, and later bare `port`; in the staged `-DWITH_UNIX_SOCKETS` build, that exact `listener` line is accepted because `atoi("tene1r")` yields `0` and the following token `892` satisfies the non-NULL Unix-socket-path requirement. No broader trigger class is claimed here.
